docs.title: Ground of Aces Modkit
docs.text:
Developer Preview - use at your own risk

This modkit is a developer preview. Everything here - the docs, the tools, the rules and the modding features of the game itself - is subject to change without notice. Anyone can read this site, but the kit itself is currently by invitation only - see "Get access" below. You use it at your own risk: back up your saves before you try a mod, and do not rely on anything here staying the way it is.

Build your own missions, quests, events, maps and more for Ground of Aces. No Unity, no compiler - a mod is a folder of text files. And if you like, an AI agent writes them for you.

I have never programmed Start here. We install everything together, step by step, and you have your first mod in the game ten minutes later.

I want to dive straight in You know your way around files and folders. Copy an example, change it, reload - done.

I use Claude Code or Codex Clone this repository, start your agent in it, and describe the mod you want. The agent knows the rules.

docs.title: Get access
docs.text: The documentation is open to everyone. The modkit itself - the repository with the examples, templates, validator and AI rules - is private during the preview. To get access, send a short email with your GitHub username to nuria@blindflugstudios.com or moritz@blindflugstudios.com. Tell us what you would like to build - we love to hear it.

docs.title: What you can build
docs.text: What it is Start with Missions Flights the player sends planes on, with four possible endings Missions Chains and campaigns Missions that unlock each other, historic operations on their real date Chains and campaigns Event scripts Python that reacts to what happens on the base and in the air Scripting Quests Checklists that guide the player Quests Game data Aircraft, buildings, raids, costs - change the numbers CSV tables Maps and art Your own maps, models, terrain objects and biomes Maps Workshop Share your mod with every player Steam Workshop

docs.title: How it works in one minute
docs.text:
1. Open the game, go to Main menu → Mods → Open folder.
  2. Put a mod folder there - for example a copy of one of the examples.
  3. Back in the game, return to the main menu, open Mods once (it rescans the folder) and load your save.

That is the whole loop - see Testing and reloading for the details. Everything else on this site is about what you put into that folder.

docs.title: Join the squadron
docs.text:
• Questions, ideas, showing off: the Discord modding channel
  • Found a mistake on this site? Open an issue or improve the page yourself with the pencil icon at the top.
  • Finished mod? Put it on the Steam Workshop.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Complete, working mods to read, copy and change. Each folder in examples/ has its own README explaining what to look at.

The fastest way to your own mission: copy coastal_patrol, rename the files and the id, and change the numbers and the text.

docs.title: The examples, roughly in order of ambition
docs.text: Folder What it is coastal_patrol One mission: a JSON file and a small script. Start here. It is the finished result of Write your first mission. raf_collection Five standalone missions, each showing a different mechanic. Three carry their text in the JSON and need no script. night_interception is the long worked example, with the handler model explained line by line. event_script Python that reacts to the base and to missions you did not write. No mission of its own. See Events. chain_convoy A fork: one mission leading to either of two others, depending on how it ended. chain_airfield A chain four deep, all of it in JSON. campaign_kanalkampf A campaign with a memory: conditions JSON cannot express, because they involve counting. script_only_scramble A mission with no JSON at all, gating and scaling itself from Python. quests Three quest files: a simple starter quest, a follow-up quest, and a quest that belongs to one map. See Quests.

docs.title: Chain or campaign?
docs.text:
The two mission sets at the bottom of the list are worth comparing.

Chain (chain_convoy, chain_airfield) Campaign (campaign_kanalkampf) Asks "did mission X succeed?" "how many times?", "who was aboard?", "what did the player choose?" Built with JSON requirements (CompletedMission) a script that decides, plus a state file Memory none: plays the same way every time remembers across flights, days and sessions Survives save and load yes, by itself yes, because the script writes its state to a file Needs Python no (the scripts in the chain examples only carry text) yes

A chain asks one yes-or-no question about the mission before, and JSON can do that on its own. A campaign asks about the whole run, and that needs a script and somewhere to keep state. Chains and campaigns explains both.

docs.title: Using an example
docs.text:
1. Copy the example folder's files into the Missions/ folder of a mod: Mods/my_mod/Missions/. (The quests example is laid out as a whole mod; copy the folder itself into Mods/.)
  2. Rename the ids. The examples use short ids like coastal_patrol because they are documentation. A real mod prefixes every id with its name (mymod_coastal_patrol), and changes it everywhere it appears: the file names, MISSION_ID in the script, CompletedMission values, and CreateMission calls.
  3. Run the validator over your mod folder (see Without an AI agent).
  4. Load a save and check the result, see Testing and reloading.

An example id that matches a built-in mission would replace it. None of the examples does, but your renamed copy should not either.

docs.title: How far each example has been tested
docs.text:
Every example has been loaded by the game. How far each was taken differs:

Example Tested coastal_patrol loaded and created in the game; not yet flown to the end raf_collection all five created in the game; night_interception flown to the end event_script handlers confirmed to fire from a mod's Missions/ folder chain_convoy loaded and created in the game; the branch not yet flown chain_airfield the unlocking confirmed in the game; the flights not yet played through in sequence campaign_kanalkampf flown in the game; the difficulty scaling measured across several raids script_only_scramble not yet tested in the game

"Loaded" means the game read the files and create_mission produced the mission with the written values; "flown" means a squadron took off and the outcome was observed.

docs.title: AI agents
docs.text:
You can build every mod on this site by hand. But you do not have to. This repository is set up so that an AI coding agent - Claude Code or Codex - can build mods for you: you describe the idea in plain words, the agent writes the files, checks them and puts them into your game.

This costs money

Claude Code needs a paid Claude subscription (Pro or higher). Codex needs a ChatGPT plan that includes it. Everything else here is free. If you do not want to pay, build your mod without an AI agent - the in-game Mission Editor is a good start.

docs.title: Why it works well here
docs.text:
A general AI knows nothing about Ground of Aces. This repository teaches it:

  • AGENTS.md is the rulebook every agent reads first: how a mod is built, where the game keeps its files on your computer, and every trap that crashes the game or fails silently.
  • Skills are step-by-step recipes for one job each - a new mission, a quest, an event script, a Workshop upload. The agent picks the right one from what you ask.
  • The validator checks the agent's work before it reaches your game. The agent runs it on its own and fixes what it finds.
  • The docs and examples on this site sit right next to it in the same folder, so the agent reads the real rules instead of guessing.

docs.title: The loop
docs.text:
1. You: "Make me a mission where ..."
  2. The agent asks what it needs to know, one question at a time.
  3. It writes the mod into mods/<your mod>/ and runs the validator until it is clean.
  4. It copies the mod into the game's Mods folder.
  5. You: in the game, go back to the main menu, open Mods once and load your save (see Testing and reloading). The cheat console command create_mission <id> makes a new mission appear right away.
  6. Tell the agent what you see. If something is off, it reads your Player.log and fixes it.

The agent cannot press buttons in the game for you - step 5 is always yours.

docs.title: Pick your agent
docs.text:
Claude Code Codex Made by Anthropic OpenAI Needs Claude Pro or higher a ChatGPT plan with Codex Reads CLAUDE.md (which loads AGENTS.md), .claude/skills/, .claude/agents/ AGENTS.md, .agents/skills/ Setup Claude Code Codex

Both use the same rules and the same skills. See Skills and agents for what is included.

docs.title: Claude Code
docs.text: Claude Code is Anthropic's coding agent. It runs in a terminal window, inside the folder you start it in, and can read, write and run files there.

docs.title: Set up
docs.text:
If you followed Install on Windows or Install on Mac, you are ready. Otherwise, in short:

WindowsMac 
winget install --id Git.Git -e
winget install --id GitHub.cli -e
winget install Anthropic.ClaudeCode

brew install git gh
brew install --cask claude-code

Then get the kit and start Claude in it:

gh repo clone blindflugstudios/goa-modkit
cd goa-modkit
claude

The first time, Claude opens your browser so you can log in with your Claude account.

docs.title: What Claude finds in this folder
docs.text: File What it does CLAUDE.md Loaded automatically. It pulls in AGENTS.md, the full rulebook. .claude/skills/ One recipe per job. Claude uses them on its own when your request matches. .claude/agents/mod-reviewer.md A second pair of eyes: checks a finished mod against every rule without changing it. .claude/agents/translator.md Translates your mod's texts, keeping ids and placeholders intact.

docs.title: Good first requests
docs.text:
Make me a mission where two Spitfires escort a damaged bomber home over the Channel.

Write an event script: when a pilot comes back from a successful mission, the crew's mood goes up a little.

Review my mod in mods/channel_escort and tell me what could go wrong.

Translate the texts of mods/channel_escort into German.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Start Claude inside the goa-modkit folder. Started anywhere else, it does not see the rules.
  • Say what you see in the game, in your own words. "The mission never shows up" is enough - Claude knows where to look.
  • Keep the kit current: ask Claude to "update the kit", or run git pull yourself. Your own mods in mods/ are never touched.

docs.title: Codex
docs.text: Codex is OpenAI's coding agent. The Codex CLI runs in a terminal inside the folder you start it in. It reads the same rules as Claude Code.

docs.title: Set up
docs.text:
Install Git and the GitHub CLI as described in Install on Windows or Install on Mac, then install the Codex CLI following OpenAI's instructions. On the first start, choose "Sign in with ChatGPT".

gh repo clone blindflugstudios/goa-modkit
cd goa-modkit
codex

docs.title: What Codex finds in this folder
docs.text:
File What it does AGENTS.md Read automatically. The full rulebook: how mods are built, where your game keeps its files, every trap. .agents/skills/ One recipe per job (new mission, quest, event script, Workshop upload ...). Codex picks the one that matches your request.

The requests and tips on the Claude Code page work the same way in Codex.

docs.title: Skills and agents
docs.text:
A skill is a written recipe for one job. The agent reads only the short description of each skill until your request matches one, then follows it step by step. Every skill that builds something ends the same way: run the validator, fix what it reports, copy the mod into the game, and tell you how to see it in the game.

The skills live in .agents/skills/ (read by Codex) and are mirrored to .claude/skills/ (read by Claude Code). They are identical.

docs.title: Skills
docs.text: Skill Say something like What it does new-mission "Make a mission where ..." Builds a mission (JSON and Python), with all four endings new-quest "Add a quest that asks the player to ..." Builds a quest with its sub-quests event-script "When X happens on the base, do Y" Writes a Python event script csv-tweak "Make the Spitfire faster" Changes game data through a CSV override localize-mod "Add German texts to my mod" Adds or fixes the texts of a mod in more languages new-map "Ship a map with my own quest line" Sets up a map folder and its metadata import-model "Use my own model for ..." Brings a 3D model into a mod publish-workshop "Put my mod on the Workshop" Checks the mod and walks you through the in-game upload validate "Check my mod" Runs the validator and explains every finding in plain words install-mod "Put my mod into the game" Copies the mod into the game's Mods folder read-log "Something is wrong, look at the log" Reads your Player.log and explains what failed update-kit "Update the kit" Pulls the newest rules, docs and skills, and tells you what changed

docs.title: Agents (Claude Code)
docs.text: Agent What it does mod-reviewer Checks a finished mod against every rule and runs the validator. Reports, never edits. translator Translates a mod's player-facing texts and keeps ids, keys and placeholders untouched.

docs.title: Write your own skill
docs.text:
A skill is a folder with a SKILL.md:

---
name: my-skill
description: One sentence saying exactly when to use this skill.
---

# My skill

Step-by-step instructions for the agent.

Put it in .agents/skills/my-skill/, run python tools/sync_skills.py to mirror it for Claude Code, and try it. Good skills are welcome as a pull request - see CONTRIBUTING.md.

docs.title: Cheat console
docs.text: The cheat console is a small command window inside the game. For modders it is the fastest way to test: create your mission right now instead of waiting days for it, jump to the quest you are working on, or skip ahead in time.

docs.title: Switch it on and open it
docs.text:
1. Load a save or start a game. The console only works while a game is running.
  2. Open Options and switch on Cheats.
  3. A cheat button appears on the game screen. Click it to open the console.

Type a command into the Enter cheat... field and press Enter. The answer appears above the field.

Key Does Enter Run the command Tab Complete the command name, and for many commands the next argument (mission ids, quest ids, resources ...) Up / Down Step through commands you typed before

Type help for the full list with an example for each command, or help create_mission for one command. Command names are not case-sensitive.

Cheats change your save

Whatever a cheat does is saved with your game. Test mods on a spare save, not on your favourite campaign.

Reloading your mod is not a console command

After changing a mod: Options → Quit to main menu, open Mods, then load your save. Quests are re-read too; only models and textures need a full game restart. See Testing and reloading.

docs.title: The commands
docs.text: Arguments in [brackets] are placeholders: replace them, without the brackets. Commands marked ★ are the ones you will use most when testing mods.

docs.title: Missions and quests
docs.text: Command What it does Example ★ create_mission [mission_id] Creates that mission right away, so it shows up on the war map without waiting. Answers Unknown mission ID if the game did not load it. create_mission coastal_patrol ★ quest [quest_id] Starts the quest with that id. quest quest3 ★ go_to_quest [quest_id] Completes quests one after another until that quest is reached. go_to_quest quest5 ★ complete_current_quests Completes the running quests (not tutorial or skin quests). complete_current_quests enable_tutorial [true/false] Turns the tutorial on or off. enable_tutorial false set_game_goals_visibility [ShowAll/ShowPriority/Minimized] Changes how the goals panel is shown. set_game_goals_visibility ShowAll

docs.title: Time and days
docs.text: Command What it does Example ★ skip_day Jumps to the next day. Good for missions with a minimum day. skip_day ★ set_day [day of week] [hour] [minute] Moves to a day of the current week. set_day Friday go_to_day_phase [Work/Leisure/Sleep] Jumps to the start of the next day phase. This also freezes the clock: follow it with freeze_time off. go_to_day_phase Leisure force_day_phase [Work/Leisure/Sleep/off] Keeps the base in one day phase until you pass off. force_day_phase Work freeze_time [hour] [minute] Holds the time of day while days keep counting. off unfreezes. freeze_time 12 0

docs.title: Base, rank and unlocks
docs.text: Command What it does Example ★ list_airstrips Lists your airstrips and their ids. list_airstrips ★ set_airstrip_tier [airstrip_id] [tier] Sets one airstrip's tier. Missions can require a runway tier. set_airstrip_tier [id] 2 ★ set_all_airstrips_tier [tier] Sets the tier of every airstrip. set_all_airstrips_tier 3 ★ set_air_base_rank [rank] Sets the air base rank. set_air_base_rank 2 set_victory_points [amount] Sets your victory points. set_victory_points 50 unlock [id] Unlocks one entry by id. Tab suggests ids. unlock [id] unlock_all_skins Unlocks all airplane skins. unlock_all_skins add_resource_pile [resource] [x] [y] [true/false] Drops an endless pile of a resource at the mouse cursor, or at a map position. Pass false last for a normal pile. add_resource_pile Tarp 10 30 false start_shipment [type] [amount] ... Sends a delivery truck. Without arguments it brings the shipment set in the HQ window. start_shipment Tarp 20 storage_blacklist_override [true/false] When on, storages block all resources by default. storage_blacklist_override false enable_crates_interaction [true/false] Allows or blocks harvesting and deconstructing crates. enable_crates_interaction true enable_equipment_deconstruction [true/false] Allows or blocks deconstructing equipment. enable_equipment_deconstruction true set_growing_time [hours] [x] [y] Sets the remaining growing time of a plant under the cursor or at a position. set_growing_time 1 fill_grave Fills a random empty grave. fill_grave

docs.title: Planes
docs.text: Command What it does Example ★ spawn_plane [plane_id] [x] [y] Adds a new plane with a pilot. Without a position it comes in to land. spawn_plane [plane_id] set_airplane_fuel [0-100] Sets fuel. set_airplane_fuel 100 set_airplane_health [0-100] Sets plane health. set_airplane_health 100 set_airplane_integrity [0-100] Sets plane integrity. set_airplane_integrity 100 destroy_airplane [airplane_id] Removes a plane. destroy_airplane [id] plane_fire Sets a random plane on fire. plane_fire spawn_plane_crash [airplane_id] Plays a crash for that plane. spawn_plane_crash [id] landing_queue_event [Wobbly/Overshoot/Smoked/Burning/Crash] The next arriving plane lands with that event. landing_queue_event Wobbly set_max_scramble_damage [amount] Caps the damage a scrambling plane can take. set_max_scramble_damage 10

docs.title: Crew and morale
docs.text: Command What it does Example ★ deliver_crew [count] [Male/Female] Sends a truck with new crew (default 2). deliver_crew 4 spawn_character [role] [male/female] [true/false] [x] [y] Spawns a crew member at the cursor or a position. Role is an air crew role, or none for ground crew. spawn_character none female set_crew_morale [Confidence/Mood/Energy] [-100..100] Sets one morale value for everyone. With only a number, sets all values. random scatters them. set_crew_morale Confidence 100 freeze_morale [true/false] Stops morale from changing. freeze_morale true set_morale_flag [add/sub] [flag] [character_id] Adds or removes a morale flag (happy, sad, angry ...) on one crew member. set_morale_flag add [flag] [id] set_crisis [Confidence/Mood/Energy] [character_id] Sends one crew member into a crisis: panic, rage or exhaustion. set_crisis Confidence [id] set_character_health [character_id] [health] Sets one crew member's health. set_character_health [id] 100 set_invulnerable_characters [true/false] Crew take no damage. set_invulnerable_characters true injure_random_character [count] Badly injures random crew. injure_random_character 1 character_fire [count] Sets random crew on fire. character_fire 1 poison Gives random crew mushroom poisoning. poison destroy_character [name] Removes a crew member. destroy_character [name] spawn_dogs [count] Adds dogs at random spawn points. spawn_dogs 3

docs.title: Attacks, fire and damage
docs.text: Command What it does Example attack [severity] Starts a base attack now. Pass a severity, or an exact mix like fighters=6 divers=4 bombers=3. attack 3 schedule_attack [day of week / +hours] Schedules a base attack for a day, or in a number of hours. schedule_attack +2 show_grid / show_grid off Draws the attack grid (A1 to P16) on the ground. show_grid grid_info [square] Lists what is on the grid squares, or on one square. grid_info G6 attack_square [square] [divers=] [bombers=] Attacks one grid square. attack_square G6 divers=3 bombers=2 get_attack_severity Prints the current attack severity. get_attack_severity bomb [x] [y] Drops a bomb at a position or the cursor. bomb 20 40 bomber_mode [true/false] Left click drops a bomb, right click a dive bomb. bomber_mode true explode [x] [y] Explosion effects at a position. explode 10 30 explode_prop [build_id] Blows up a placed prop or workbench, for example Kitchen. explode_prop Kitchen fire [x] [y] [count] Starts fires at a position, at random places (count only), or at the cursor. fire 5 disable_fires [true/false] Stops fires from starting and spreading. disable_fires true target Makes aiming planes target the thing under the cursor. target

docs.title: Map settings
docs.text:
These change the settings you choose when starting a map. The number is the setting's level.

Command What it does Example attacks_rate_parameter [value] Attack frequency setting. attacks_rate_parameter 1 change_attack_severity_parameter [value] Attack severity shift setting. change_attack_severity_parameter 1 change_harvest_rate_parameter [value] Harvest rate setting. change_harvest_rate_parameter 1 change_resource_degradation_rate_parameter [value] Resource decay setting. change_resource_degradation_rate_parameter 1 explosion_damage_rate_parameter [value] Explosion damage setting. explosion_damage_rate_parameter 1 hq_strikes_parameter [value] HQ requirement setting. hq_strikes_parameter 0 set_random_event_chance [0-1] Base chance of random events. set_random_event_chance 0.5

docs.title: Debug views and technical
docs.text:
Use these only if you know why. enable_system and enable_input_action can leave a save in a strange state.

Command What it does Example show_attack_heatmap Shows where attacks will aim. show_attack_heatmap show_voxel_owners / show_voxel_owners off Shows which object owns each tile. show_voxel_owners damage_debug [true/false] Visualizes explosion damage. damage_debug true set_target_fps [fps] Caps the frame rate. set_target_fps 30 enable_input_action [map/action] [true/false] Turns one input action on or off. enable_input_action Game/TimeScalePause false enable_system [name] [true/false] Turns one internal game process on or off. enable_system [name] false

docs.title: A typical test run
docs.text:
create_mission coastal_patrol
set_all_airstrips_tier 3
deliver_crew 4
skip_day

Create your mission, make sure the base meets its requirements, get enough crew, and move on a day to see what happens next.

docs.title: How mods work
docs.text:
A mod is a folder. The game looks inside it for a handful of fixed subfolders, and whatever those subfolders contain is what the mod changes. There is no packaging step, no manifest you have to write, and nothing to compile: you edit files, load a level, and see the result.

This page covers what every mod has in common: where it lives, how the game finds it, how it is switched on and off, and which mod wins when two change the same thing. What goes into the subfolders is on the category pages: CSV tables, Missions, Quests, Scripting and the Maps and art pages. How a finished mod reaches other players is on Steam Workshop.

docs.title: A mod in one minute
docs.text:
1. Find your Mods folder: Main menu → Mods → Open folder. On Windows that is %USERPROFILE%\AppData\LocalLow\Blindflug Studios\Ground Of Aces\Mods\; the other platforms are listed below.
  2. Create a folder in it, for example my_mod, and inside it one of the content folders: CSV/, Missions/, Quests/, Maps/, Objects/, TerrainObjects/ or Biomes/. Put at least one file in it.
  3. Optionally add a config.json with the mod's name and id, and a preview.png (at most 1 MB) as its picture.
  4. Press Refresh in the Mods window so the game notices the new folder, then load a level.
  5. From then on, every change to a file inside the mod is picked up the next time you load a level.

The folder can have any name - MyMod works as well as my_mod. Only the optional Id inside config.json has to be lower-case (my_mod, not MyMod). Prefix every id you invent with your mod's name, so you never replace something by accident.

Tip

If this is your first mod, the shortest path from an empty folder to a visible change is a one-line CSV table change. The first mod walkthrough takes you through it step by step.

docs.title: Where mods live
docs.text:
The game reads mods from two places: the items you are subscribed to on the Steam Workshop, and your own Mods folder. Anything you make yourself goes into the second one.

Platform Mods folder Windows %USERPROFILE%\AppData\LocalLow\Blindflug Studios\Ground Of Aces\Mods\ macOS ~/Library/Application Support/Blindflug Studios/Ground Of Aces/Mods/ Linux ~/.config/unity3d/Blindflug Studios/Ground Of Aces/Mods/

The folder is created the first time the game starts. The quickest way to reach it is the Open folder button in the Mods window (see below). The game also keeps a small mod_state.json in this folder. That file is the game's own record of which mods you switched on or off; it is not part of any mod, and you should not ship it.

docs.title: One mod is one folder
docs.text:
The folder can have any name you like - MyMod, my_mod or My Campaign all work. The lower-case rule further down applies only to the optional Id inside config.json, not to the folder.

Inside your mod's folder, each kind of content has a fixed subfolder. Only the ones you need have to exist:

Mods/
  my_mod/
    config.json        optional - name, id, load order
    preview.png        optional - the picture shown in the Mods window and on the Workshop
    CSV/               data tables
    Missions/          mission .json files and Python .py scripts
    Quests/            quest .json files
    Maps/              .goamap map files
    Objects/           replacement models for buildings and objects
    TerrainObjects/    replacement models for trees, rocks and other map objects
    Biomes/            biome definitions
Folder What goes in it Read more CSV/ changes to the game's data tables CSV tables Missions/ missions (.json) and Python scripts (.py) Missions, Scripting Quests/ quests (.json) Quests Maps/ maps (.goamap) Maps Objects/ replacement models for buildings and objects Objects and models TerrainObjects/ replacement models for trees, rocks and other map objects Terrain objects Biomes/ biome definitions Biomes

Three rules decide whether the game notices the folder at all:

  • A subfolder only counts when there is something in it. An empty CSV/ folder is the same as no CSV/ folder.
  • A mod folder with none of the subfolders above (or only empty ones) is ignored without a message.
  • Symbolic links and junctions (shortcuts that point to another folder) are never followed, neither as the mod folder nor as one of its subfolders. The game skips them with a warning in the log.

For CSV, Missions, Quests and Maps only files directly inside the subfolder are read; anything deeper is ignored. Objects, TerrainObjects and Biomes work the other way round: each object gets its own subfolder named after the thing it replaces. Their pages explain the layout.

docs.title: config.json
docs.text:
Optional. Without it, the folder name is shown as the mod's name, its id is made from the folder name, and the load order is 100.

{
  "Id": "my_mod",
  "Name": "My Mod",
  "Author": "Your Name",
  "Version": "1.0.0",
  "LoadOrder": 100
}
Field Meaning Id What the game uses to tell mods apart and to break load-order ties. 3–64 characters of lower-case letters, digits, _, . or -, starting with a letter or digit. Name What players see in the Mods window. Any text. It also becomes the Workshop title on a first upload. LoadOrder A whole number that decides the order in which mods are applied (see Which mod wins). Lower numbers are applied first. Default 100. Author, Version Kept for you and for anyone reading the file. The game does not read them.

What happens when something is off:

  • An Id that breaks the rule is ignored without a message, and the folder name is used instead - lower-cased, with every character other than letters, digits, _, . and - replaced by _. Log lines about your mod are labelled with this id, so a rejected id shows up as a label you did not expect. The mod's details view in the Mods window also shows the id the game actually uses.
  • A config.json the game cannot read (a missing comma, a stray bracket) is reported in the log and treated as if it were absent.

docs.title: preview.png
docs.text: Optional. A PNG at the root of the mod folder, at most 1 MB. The Mods window shows it next to the mod's name, and it becomes the item's picture when you upload the mod to the Workshop. Without one the Mods window shows a placeholder picture.

docs.title: The Mods window
docs.text:
Main menu → Mods lists every mod the game found - Workshop subscriptions and your own folders - with its preview picture, a marker that says whether it came from the Workshop or from your Mods folder, and one badge per kind of content it carries.

Control What it does Enabled switch (per mod) Switches the mod on or off. A mod that is off contributes nothing: its tables, quests, missions, scripts and maps are all skipped. Maps take effect at once; everything else the next time a level is loaded. New mods are on by default. Upload button (per mod, your own mods only) Publishes the mod to the Steam Workshop. See Steam Workshop. Refresh Scans the Workshop items and your Mods folder again. Press it after you create a new mod folder, rename one, change a config.json, or subscribe to something on the Workshop while the game is running. Open folder Opens your Mods folder in the file browser, creating it if it does not exist yet. Workshop Opens the game's Steam Workshop page in the Steam overlay (Steam version only).

Each mod also has a details view that shows its name, the id the game uses, its load order and the folder it was read from, with a button to open that folder.

Mods that contain Python files also show a Scripting switch. Turning it on asks you to confirm. At the moment the game does not enforce this switch, so it is no protection: a mod's scripts run whenever the mod is enabled, whatever the switch says. The only way to keep a mod's scripts from running is to switch the whole mod off. Read Python mods and safety before you enable a mod with scripts from someone you do not know.

docs.title: Which mod wins
docs.text:
Mods are applied Workshop items first, then the ones in your Mods folder, and inside each group in LoadOrder order - lower numbers first, ties broken by id. When two mods provide the same thing - a row in the same table, a quest with the same file name, a mission with the same id - the one applied last wins. Two consequences:

  • Your own copy of a mod always beats the Workshop copy of the same mod. You can keep working on a mod you have already published and test your changes with the published version still subscribed.
  • Two mods from the same place (both Workshop, or both in your Mods folder) with the same id are not both loaded. The second one found is skipped with a warning in the log.

The practical rule that follows: prefix every id you invent with your mod's name, so you never replace something by accident.

Your own Missions and Maps folders next to Mods - where the in-game Mission Editor and the map editor save - follow different rules:

  • Missions: your own Missions folder is read after every mod and wins over all of them. Remember that folder when a mission of yours seems to ignore the copy in your mod.
  • Maps: the order is the other way round. Maps are read shipped maps first, then your own Maps folder, then the enabled mods in load order. So a mod map with the same file name replaces both your own map and the shipped one. See Maps.

docs.title: Seeing your changes
docs.text:
Everything a mod contains is read when a level is loaded. Return to the main menu and load a save or start a map, and the game picks up whatever you changed in the meantime - tables, quests, missions, scripts and maps alike. The list of mods is scanned when the game starts, whenever you open the Mods window, and when you press Refresh there.

The everyday loop while you work on a mod:

  1. Save your game.
  2. Options → Quit to main menu.
  3. Open Mods if you added or renamed a mod folder (opening the window scans again).
  4. Load the save.
You changed... To see it A file inside a mod the game already knows Load a level (loading a save is enough) A map inside a mod Also at once, when you toggle the mod's Enabled switch A new mod folder, a renamed folder, a changed config.json, a subfolder that was empty when the game started Open the Mods window (or press Refresh there), then load a level - or restart the game A new Workshop subscription while the game is running Refresh in the Mods window once Steam has finished downloading it

Testing and reloading has more on this loop and on the tools that help while testing.

The game writes what it accepted and what it refused to its log file, Player.log:

Platform Log file Windows %USERPROFILE%\AppData\LocalLow\Blindflug Studios\Ground Of Aces\Player.log macOS ~/Library/Logs/Blindflug Studios/Ground Of Aces/Player.log Linux ~/.config/unity3d/Blindflug Studios/Ground Of Aces/Player.log

The previous run's log is kept next to it as Player-prev.log. The released game writes mainly errors to the log, so some of the detailed [Mod ...] lines described on the category pages may not appear there; when in doubt, check the effect in the game itself. More on this in Testing and reloading and When nothing happens.

docs.title: Python mods and safety
docs.text: Short version: a mod with Python scripts is a small program running on your computer. Install script mods only from people you trust, and as a modder, never write scripts that reach outside the game.

docs.title: What the risk is
docs.text:
Mods that only contain JSON, CSV, maps or models are data. The game reads them, and the worst a broken one can do is break your game.

Mods with Python scripts (.py files) are different. The game runs them with IronPython, and there is no sandbox: the game does not stop a script from importing whatever it likes. A script can reach the .NET runtime and the file system, which means a badly meant script could read, change or delete files on your computer.

We are telling you this plainly because you should know it, not because Workshop mods are dangerous as a rule. The same is true for mods in most games that allow scripting.

docs.title: For players
docs.text:
• Know which mods have scripts. The Mods window shows which mods contain scripts.
  • Only use script mods from authors you trust: people you know from the community, with a history of mods, comments and a Workshop page that explains what the mod does.
  • Subscribed Workshop mods are switched on by default. You can switch any mod off in the Mods window.
  • The game asks before you turn on scripting for a mod. Take that question seriously. If you are not sure about the author, say no, or unsubscribe.
  • Something odd? Unsubscribe, and report the mod on its Workshop page and in the modding channel on Discord.

Check a mod before you trust it

Every Workshop mod is a folder of plain-text files. You can open its .py files in a text editor, or run the modkit's validator on the folder: it reads the scripts without running them and warns about anything that reaches outside the game.

docs.title: For modders
docs.text:
Your mod never needs anything outside the game's scripting API. Stick to it, and your players never have to wonder.

Normal and fine: the game's own scripting API, including imports from the game's Blindflug.* namespaces and the objects the game hands every script:

from Blindflug.FlightMission import MissionEvent
from Blindflug.GameResources import ResourceType

localization.SetTerm("en", "missions/my_mission/mission_name", "Dawn Patrol")

Never use these. The validator warns about each of them:

Import or call Why it is off limits import clr The bridge into .NET, and from there to everything on the computer import System, from System.IO import ... (anything under System or Microsoft) Direct .NET access: files, processes, network import os, shutil, io, open(...) File system access (the validator only notes it, because of the one exception below) import sys, subprocess, ctypes, importlib Interpreter internals, starting programs, loading native code socket, urllib, http, ftplib, smtplib Network access pickle, marshal, exec, eval, compile, __import__ Running code that is not visible in your file

One exception for files: if a script needs to keep its own small state between sessions, the scripting API hands out a folder for that (game_api.GetScriptDataPath). Use only that folder.

docs.title: Before you publish
docs.text:
1. Run the validator and make sure there are no "reaches outside the game" warnings.
  2. Say in your Workshop description that the mod contains scripts and what they do.
  3. Keep your scripts readable. Players and reviewers can open them, and clear code builds trust.

The modkit's skills and examples follow these rules. If an agent ever suggests one of the imports above, tell it no.

docs.title: Testing and reloading
docs.text: There is no preview window for mods. You test a mod by loading it into the game and watching what happens. This page shows how to make that loop short: change a file, reload, look, without restarting the game.

docs.title: The short version
docs.text:
1. Edit your files in the mod folder.
  2. In the game, save, then Options → Quit to main menu.
  3. Open Mods from the main menu. The window rescans the Mods folder when it opens; Refresh rescans it again.
  4. Load your save. Missions, scripts, quests and CSV tables are read fresh every time a save is loaded. Only art needs a full restart.
  5. For a mission, open the cheat console and type create_mission <your_mission_id> to put it on the war map right now.
  6. Something wrong? Open Player.log (see below).

docs.title: Reloading without restarting the game
docs.text:
Every time you load a save, the game reads your mod's content again: mission files, Python scripts, quests and CSV tables, from the game itself and from every enabled mod. So the edit loop is: change a file, go back to the main menu, open Mods, load the save again.

Two things need more:

  • Art is imported only when the game starts. Models, textures and other files in Objects/, TerrainObjects/ and Biomes/ need a full restart of the game.
  • New mods: a mod folder you just created shows up after the Mods window has rescanned (open it, or press Refresh). Check that the mod is switched on.

A mission that was already on the war map in your save keeps the values it was created with. After changing a mission's JSON, create a fresh copy with create_mission to see the change.

docs.title: Making a mission appear now
docs.text:
Missions are drawn randomly across the week, so waiting for a specific one is slow.

create_mission mymod_coastal_patrol

puts the mission on the war map immediately. The cheat console needs a loaded game: switch it on under Options → Cheats, then use the cheat button on the game screen (see Cheat console). It ignores the mission's requirements, date gates and map tags, so it proves the mission loads and flies, not that it would appear on its own. The console suggests mission ids as you type.

If the answer is Unknown mission ID, the game has not read your files: see the checklist below. If it is Mission ... has neither mission data nor a script, the file was found but could not be used, usually a script-only mission without a get_mission_id handler.

Other cheats that help while testing missions:

Command Use skip_day jump to the next day; historic missions with a date are checked at every day change freeze_time off if the clock stopped (some cheats freeze time as a side effect)

The full list is on the Cheat console page.

docs.title: Testing a chain
docs.text:
create_mission skips every gate, so it cannot show that a chain unlocks. To test the unlocking:

  1. Lower the gates for the test: RunwayTier 1 and EarliestAppearanceDay 1 remove the two most common reasons a mission never shows up.
  2. Make the follow-up historic ("_isHistoric": true). Historic missions skip the random draw and appear at the next weekly slot, or on their date, as soon as their gates pass.
  3. Fly the first mission to the outcome you are testing and wait for the next slot.

Remember that a historic mission is one-shot once it has been won. Turn _isHistoric off again afterwards if the mission is not meant to be a story beat.

docs.title: When nothing shows up
docs.text:
Work down this list before you start doubting your logic.

1. Is the file in the right place? Mission files, event scripts and helper modules all go into Mods/<your_mod>/Missions/. There is no Events/ or Scripts/ folder for mods; a script placed anywhere else never runs, silently. The extension must be exactly .py or .json (watch out for coastal_patrol.json.txt when your system hides extensions).

2. Is the mod enabled? A mod switched off in the Mods window is not loaded at all. A mod folder you created while the game was running appears after the Mods window has rescanned.

3. Did the script load? Every script that loads successfully is listed in Player.log with its file name, followed by the handlers it registered. If your file name is missing, the game did not read it.

4. Is there a syntax error? A Python syntax error shows up in Player.log as:

Python syntax error: <message> (line N, column M)

The whole file is then skipped; nothing in it registers. Mods run on IronPython 3.4: stick to the Python features the examples use, and avoid anything newer than Python 3.6 (:=, match).

5. Did the JSON parse? A broken mission file is skipped with this line in Player.log:

Mission file at <path> could not be parsed, skipping it: <reason>

A missing comma or an extra one at the end of a list is the usual cause.

6. Do the names match? The .py file name, the .json file name and the id get_mission_id returns must be identical. With a mismatch, the game runs the default script instead of yours.

7. Is the id already taken? A mission with the same id as a built-in mission, or as one in another mod, replaces it (or is replaced by it). Rename yours with a prefix.

8. Are the gates passing? A mission only enters the pool when all its requirements pass. Check RunwayTier against your base, EarliestAppearanceDay against the day of the campaign, CompletedMission against what has actually been flown, and _tags against the map. A chain step additionally needs its predecessor finished with the right outcome.

docs.title: The two crashes worth knowing
docs.text:
Both come from checks the game does not make, so there is no friendly message:

  • Not exactly four _missionOutcomes: the mission crashes when it finishes, long after you stopped suspecting the JSON.
  • Fewer than two _missionStats: the mission crashes on the skill roll, in the middle of the flight.

If a mission flies but blows up at the end, count the outcomes first.

docs.title: Checks you can run before launching
docs.text:
Everything below can be checked without starting the game, and is worth doing after every edit. The validator does all of it for you (see Without an AI agent):

  • the JSON parses
  • exactly 4 outcomes, in the order: gone wrong + failed, gone wrong + passed, as planned + failed, as planned + passed
  • at least 2 mission stats
  • _missionIcon is one of Fight, Recon, Bomb, Transport, Maneuverability, Stealth, Luxury, Success, Failure, Cancel
  • _enemyPlaneReport is 18 or lower
  • .py and .json share a name, and get_mission_id returns that name
  • the id does not duplicate an existing mission id
  • every text key the script writes follows missions/<id>/<slot>
  • no never-called handler is implemented (get_mission_icon, calculate_*_modifiers)

A clean validator run means the mod is well-formed, not that it plays well. Only a flight in the game tells you that.

docs.title: Where text goes missing
docs.text:
If the mission appears but shows a raw key like missions/mymod_patrol/mission_name instead of a name, that text was never defined. The game builds three keys itself and expects them to exist:

missions/<id>/mission_name
missions/<id>/mission_description
missions/<id>/intel_threat_report

They cannot be renamed. Define them with localization.SetTerm, or fill the matching _raw* fields in the JSON (see Localization). The other six keys are used by your own script, so a typo there shows up as a raw key in the event log rather than in the mission window.

docs.title: Reading Player.log
docs.text:
The game writes everything it notices into a text file called Player.log. It is rewritten each time the game starts, so look at it while the game is running or right after closing it.

Platform Location Windows %USERPROFILE%\AppData\LocalLow\Blindflug Studios\Ground Of Aces\Player.log macOS ~/Library/Logs/Blindflug Studios/Ground Of Aces/Player.log Linux ~/.config/unity3d/Blindflug Studios/Ground Of Aces/Player.log

Open it with any text editor and search for your mod name or mission id. Your own scripts can write to it with logger.Log("..."), see API.

docs.title: Biomes
docs.text:
A biome is a ground type: the grass, dirt, road, rock, sand or gravel painted across a map with the Biomes tool of the Map Editor. The game has 24 of them. A mod can repaint any of them with a new texture, and the change shows on every map, shipped or custom.

A biome mod changes the look only. How fast people and aircraft move over the ground, which runway tier it counts as, and similar rules live in the Biomes table and are changed with CSV tables.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
Give the first grass a new texture:

Mods/
  my_ground_mod/
    Biomes/
      Terrain-Type_Grass_A/
        albedo.png

Restart the game and load a save or start a map. Everywhere the map uses that grass, you now see your texture.

Note

Biome textures are read once, when the game starts. After changing a texture or switching the mod on or off, restart the game.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Biomes/ holds one folder per biome you want to repaint, named exactly after the biome (see the list). Capitalisation does not matter.
  • Each folder needs one file: albedo.png, the colour texture.
  • A mod cannot add new biomes, only repaint the 24 that exist. A map remembers which biome is painted where by number, so there is nothing a new one could be attached to.
  • The biome's surface detail and its burnt look after a fire are not replaced.
  • The game's own textures are untouched on disk. When you leave a map, the original ground returns, and switching the mod off (and restarting) brings it back everywhere.

docs.title: The texture
docs.text:
Rule Limit Format PNG only Size At most 2048 × 2048 pixels File size At most 8 MB File name albedo.png

The game scales your texture to the size of its own ground textures, so any size within the limit works; a square image avoids stretching. The texture repeats across the ground, so it should tile seamlessly: the left edge must continue into the right edge, the top into the bottom.

Other files in a biome folder (model.glb, destroyed_albedo.png, ...) mean nothing here. The log says so, and albedo.png still loads.

docs.title: Biome names
docs.text:
The number is the biome's row in the Biomes table. Rows with the same number describe how that ground plays.

Number Folder name Ground 0 Terrain-Type_Dirt_A dirt 1 Terrain-Type_Dirt_B dirt 2 Terrain-Type_Dirt_C dirt 3 Terrain-Type_Dirt_D dirt 4 Terrain-Type_Dirt_E dirt 5 Terrain-Type_Dirt_F dirt 6 Terrain-Type_Dirt_G dirt, also laid under parking spots, gardening plots and dirt runways 7 Terrain-Type_Dirt_H dirt 8 Terrain-Type_Grass_A grass 9 Terrain-Type_Grass_B grass 10 Terrain-Type_Grass_C grass 11 Terrain-Type_Grass_D grass 12 Terrain-Type_Grass_E grass 13 Terrain-Type_Road_A road, also laid under tarmac runways 14 Terrain-Type_Road_B road 15 Terrain-Type_Road_C road, also laid under concrete runways 16 Terrain-Type_Rock_A rock 17 Terrain-Type_Rock_B rock 18 Terrain-Type_Rock_C rock 19 Terrain-Type_Sand_A sand 20 Terrain-Type_Sand_B sand, also laid under sand runways 21 Terrain-Type_Sand_C sand 22 Terrain-Type_Gravel_A gravel, also laid under gravel runways 23 Terrain-Type_Grass_B3 grass

The runway surfaces are the built-in values of the AirstripTiers table (Biome Id column); a mod that changes that table changes which ground is laid.

docs.title: Biomes and the Biomes table
docs.text:
The two are independent and combine freely:

You want to change... Use What a ground type looks like Biomes/<name>/albedo.png (this page) How a ground type plays: movement speed, runway tier, wear on stored goods, fire spread The Biomes table, row <number> (CSV tables) Which ground is painted where on a map The Biomes tool in the Map Editor

docs.title: Several mods, same biome
docs.text: If two enabled mods repaint the same biome, the mod applied last wins, and the log notes which one overrode which. See How mods work for the order.

docs.title: When something does not show up
docs.text:
Check Player.log for lines starting with [Mod <your mod id>] Biomes/...:

Log line (shortened) Meaning Biomes/Terrain-Type_Grass_A: replaced biome slot 8 (Terrain-Type_Grass_A). Your texture is in use. Written when a map loads. Biomes/Grass_A names no biome of this game. Known biomes: Terrain-Type_Dirt_A, ... The folder name does not match. Copy it from the list above. Biomes/Terrain-Type_Grass_A has no albedo.png and is ignored Add the texture, or fix its name. Biomes/Terrain-Type_Grass_A: only albedo.png is used for a biome; the other files are ignored. Harmless; remove the extra files if you like. Biomes/Terrain-Type_Grass_A/albedo.png is 4096x4096, over the 2048x2048 limit Scale the texture down. Biomes/Terrain-Type_Grass_A/albedo.png is not a PNG Save it as a real PNG. [Mods] This device cannot copy textures on the GPU; biome textures from mods are not applied. Your graphics hardware does not support biome mods. Nothing to fix in the mod.

docs.title: Maps
docs.text:
A map is the patch of English countryside your airfield is built on: the shape of the ground, the fields and roads painted on it, the trees and rocks, anything already standing there, plus a few settings such as the start date and the crew you begin with. Every map is one file ending in .goamap.

You build maps with the Map Editor that comes with the game, and you ship them in a mod's Maps/ folder. A map can also decide which missions may turn up on it (through tags) and which quest line it starts with.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
1. In the main menu, click Map Editor, then New Map. Shape the ground, paint it, place some trees.
  2. Open Map settings and fill in at least Name of Location. Save the map with Save as... and call it my_airfield.
  3. The editor writes my_airfield.goamap into the Maps folder inside your game data folder (the folder that also holds Mods/, see the table below).

  4. Copy that file into a mod:

    Mods/
  my_map_mod/
    Maps/
      my_airfield.goamap

  5. Open Main menu → Mods, make sure my_map_mod is switched on, then start a new game. Your map is listed under Custom maps.

That is a complete map mod. No config.json is needed, although you may add one (see How mods work).

Platform Game data folder (holds Mods/ and Maps/) Windows %USERPROFILE%\AppData\LocalLow\Blindflug Studios\Ground Of Aces\ macOS ~/Library/Application Support/Blindflug Studios/Ground Of Aces/ Linux ~/.config/unity3d/Blindflug Studios/Ground Of Aces/

Tip

Give the file a name nobody else will pick, for example with your mod's name in front: my_map_mod_airfield.goamap. The file name is the map's id (see Map ids).

docs.title: The Map Editor
docs.text:
Click Map Editor in the main menu. A window lets you start a New Map or load an existing one.

The editor has a tool for each part of the map:

Tool What you do with it Terrain Height Raise and lower the ground. Biomes Paint the ground type: grass, dirt, road, rock, sand, gravel. The ground type also affects gameplay, see Biomes. Grass Paint grass on the ground, or remove it. Terrain Objects Place trees, bushes, rocks, ponds and so on, one by one or with a brush. See Terrain objects for the list. Map settings The name, description, tags, starting quests, start date and starting supplies of the map (see below).

Undo and Redo work as you would expect. The editor lists its keyboard shortcuts under Shortcuts.

docs.title: Saving
docs.text:
Save writes over the map you loaded, Save as... asks for a new name. Maps are saved into the Maps folder in your game data folder.

The shipped maps and maps that come from a mod are write-protected: you can load them in the editor, but you can only store your changes with Save as... under a new name. To update a map in your mod, edit the copy in your Maps folder and copy it over the one in Mods/<your mod>/Maps/ again.

docs.title: Map settings
docs.text:
Every field in Map settings is stored in the map's Metadata.json (see Reference):

Field in the editor Key in Metadata.json Notes Name of Location: Name Shown in the map list. Description: Description Shown when the map is selected. Tags _tags Comma-separated: default, my_campaign. Decides which missions may appear, see Tags and missions. Starting Quest StartingQuestIds Comma-separated quest ids: quest0, my_first_quest. See Starting quests. Designation AirplaneDesignation The squadron code used in your aircraft designations, for example DB. Coordinates Coordinates Latitude and longitude of the airfield. Starting Date (dd.mm.yyyy) StartDatetime Day first, digits and dots only: 15.08.1940. The time of day is kept. Amount of Crew Members: InitialCrewCount Crew you start with. Resource list InitialResources Supplies in stock at the start.

In the comma-separated fields, spaces around the commas are ignored and empty entries are dropped.

docs.title: What is inside a .goamap
docs.text:
A .goamap file is an ordinary zip archive with a different ending. Rename a copy to .zip (or open it with any archive tool such as 7-Zip) and you see:

File What it holds Metadata.json Name, description, tags, starting quests, dates, starting supplies. The only file you should edit by hand. Icon.png The picture shown for the map. Heightmap.bytes The shape of the ground. TerrainBiomeTexture.png Which ground type is painted where. TerrainGrassTexture.png Where grass grows. TerrainObjects.json Trees, rocks, bushes and other terrain objects. Props.json, Buildings.json, Roof.json, Workbenches.json, TrainingObjects.json, FunctionAreas.json Everything already built on the map. Airplanes.json, Characters.json Aircraft and people placed on the map.

Leave everything except Metadata.json to the Map Editor.

docs.title: Editing Metadata.json by hand
docs.text:
You can change tags and starting quests without opening the editor:

  1. Open the .goamap with an archive tool.
  2. Extract Metadata.json, edit it in a text editor, and put it back into the archive under the same name.
  3. Keep the archive's file name and the .goamap ending.

Here are the keys you would typically touch, with a tag and a quest line of your own. The real file holds more keys; leave those as they are:

{
  "Name": "Little Snoring",
  "Description": "A grass strip in Norfolk, two fields and a pub.",
  "AirplaneDesignation": "LS",
  "_tags": [
    "my_campaign"
  ],
  "StartingQuestIds": [
    "my_campaign_arrival"
  ]
}

Warning

Keep the file valid JSON: no comments, no trailing commas. A map whose Metadata.json cannot be read is left out of the map list.

docs.title: Tags and missions
docs.text:
Tags are free-form labels that link maps and missions. A map lists the tags it supports in _tags, a mission lists the tags it is written for in its own _tags, and the mission can only appear on the map when the two lists share at least one tag.

  • Tags ignore capitalisation: My_Campaign and my_campaign match.
  • A missing or empty list counts as the single tag default, on the map and on the mission alike.
  • Every shipped map lists default and its own name: debden, duxford, lichfield, perranporth. So an untagged mission appears on all of them, and a mission tagged only duxford appears only on Duxford.

What that means for your map:

Your map's _tags Missions that can appear missing or [] Every untagged mission and every mission tagged default. ["default", "my_campaign"] All of the above, plus missions tagged my_campaign. ["my_campaign"] Only missions tagged my_campaign. The regular missions stay away.

Tags only affect missions. Quests are not tagged; a map chooses its quests with StartingQuestIds. How to tag a mission is explained in Missions.

docs.title: Starting quests
docs.text:
StartingQuestIds lists the quests the map hands out when it is loaded, whatever those quests' own requirements say. When the list is missing or empty, the map starts the game's default quest line, quest0, so no map is ever without quests.

"StartingQuestIds": ["my_campaign_arrival"]

As soon as you list your own quest, quest0 is no longer started on that map, and the shipped main quest line stays away. If you want both, list both:

"StartingQuestIds": ["quest0", "my_campaign_arrival"]

An id that no quest file provides is skipped; the map still loads. How to write the quests themselves is covered in Quests.

docs.title: Map ids
docs.text:
A map's id is its file name without .goamap. my_airfield.goamap has the id my_airfield, and saves remember the map by that id.

  • Only files directly inside Maps/ are read. Subfolders are ignored.
  • Two maps with the same id do not both appear. The one read last replaces the other. Maps are read in this order: the shipped maps, your own Maps folder, then the enabled mods in load order. So a mod map named Debden.goamap replaces the shipped Debden. Pick a unique name unless that is exactly what you want.
  • If a mod map replaces a map, saves made on that map load the mod's version.

docs.title: Seeing your changes
docs.text:
You changed... To see it A map file inside a mod the game already knows Switch the mod off and on again in Main menu → Mods. Maps are re-read at once. A new mod folder, or a Maps/ folder that was empty when the game started Press Refresh in the Mods window, or restart the game. A map you saved in the Map Editor Nothing to do, the map list is re-read when you save. A .goamap in your own Maps folder that you edited by hand Restart the game.

If in doubt, restart the game. More on the test loop in Testing and reloading.

docs.title: Metadata.json reference
docs.text:
Keys you may edit, by hand or through Map settings:

Key Type Default when missing What it does Name text none Name shown in the map list. Plain text, or a localization key. Description text none Description shown when the map is selected. Plain text, or a localization key. _tags list of text ["default"] Tags this map supports. Matched against the _tags of missions. StartingQuestIds list of text ["quest0"] Quests handed out when the map loads. An empty list also means ["quest0"]. AirplaneDesignation text none Squadron code for your aircraft designations. Coordinates object { "x": latitude, "y": longitude } none Where the airfield is on the globe. InitialCrewCount whole number 0 Crew at the start. StartDatetime date and time, "1940-08-15T07:00:00" 15 August 1940, 07:00 When the game starts. BaseOpeningDatetime date and time 1 August 1940, 00:00 Opening date of the base, shown before the game starts. InitialResources object, resource name to amount none Supplies at the start, for example { "Planks": 50, "Fuel": 15 }.

The editor also writes keys such as CreatedDatetime, ModifiedDatetime, AirCrewCount, AirplanesCount, AirstripsCount, DeliveryTruckWaypoints, ShipmentSpawningLocation and DogSpawnPositions. Leave them as the editor wrote them.

docs.title: Sharing a map
docs.text: Your own maps can be uploaded to the Steam Workshop straight from the map list in the Map Editor, and whole mods from the Mods window. See Steam Workshop.

docs.title: Objects and models
docs.text:
Tired of the standard-issue barrel? A mod can give the objects you build on your airfield a new look: furniture, fences, guns, signs, posters, workbenches and training equipment. You either drop in a new 3D model, or keep the game's model and paint it with a new texture.

Only the look changes. Size on the grid, cost, what crew can do with the object, and every other rule stay as the game defines them. Changing numbers is done with CSV tables.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
Give the barrel a new model. Export your model as a binary glTF file named model.glb and put it here:

Mods/
  my_barrel_mod/
    Objects/
      Barrel/
        model.glb

Restart the game and load a save. Every barrel, the ones already standing and new ones you build, now uses your model.

Just want to recolour the existing barrel? Put a texture next to nothing else:

Mods/
  my_barrel_mod/
    Objects/
      Barrel/
        albedo.png

The game keeps its own barrel model and paints your albedo.png onto it instead of the original texture.

Note

Models and textures are read once, when the game starts. After you change a file, switching a mod on or off, or adding a new object folder, restart the game. Loading a save is not enough for art.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
Inside your mod, the Objects/ folder holds one subfolder per object you want to change. The subfolder's name is the object's id (see Which objects can be changed); capitalisation does not matter.

Each object folder may contain these files. All of them are optional, but a folder needs at least one of the first four:

File What it does model.glb or model.fbx Replaces the object's model. albedo.png The colour texture. With a model: painted onto your model. Without a model: painted onto the game's own model. destroyed.glb or destroyed.fbx Replaces the model shown after the object has been destroyed, for example by a bombing raid. destroyed_albedo.png The colour texture for the destroyed look, following the same rules as albedo.png. config.json Settings for this object (see config.json).

Everything else on the object stays as the game made it: where crew stand to use it, the space it takes, fire and smoke effects, sounds. The ghost preview you see while placing the object already shows your model.

docs.title: Two ways to reskin
docs.text:
New model. Your model replaces the game's model entirely. Its origin is placed exactly where the original model sits, with no rotation or scaling added. Model your object to the same size and facing as the original: look at the original in the game, and build yours on the same footprint.

Texture only. Without a model file, albedo.png replaces the colour texture on every material of the game's model. The game's model is mapped to its own texture layout, so your texture has to follow that layout to look right. This is best for recolouring: a darker tint, a different paint scheme, weathering.

docs.title: The destroyed look
docs.text: Many objects switch to a wrecked look when they are destroyed. destroyed.glb / destroyed.fbx and destroyed_albedo.png change that look in the same two ways. If an object has no destroyed look at all, those files are skipped and the log says so. If you leave them out, the object keeps the game's own destroyed look.

docs.title: Model formats
docs.text:
Format File name Notes glTF binary model.glb, destroyed.glb Recommended. Materials and embedded textures are used as authored. FBX model.fbx, destroyed.fbx Meshes and material colours only. Textures inside the FBX are not read; ship an albedo.png next to it.

If a folder has both model.glb and model.fbx, the .glb is used and the log mentions the .fbx it ignored.

docs.title: glTF (.glb)
docs.text:
• Only the binary form, .glb, is read. A .gltf text file with separate .bin and image files is not.
  • The file must be self-contained. A .glb that points to outside files or web addresses has those references refused. Embed textures into the .glb when you export (Blender's glTF exporter does this with the format set to glTF Binary).
  • Materials use the standard glTF metallic-roughness model. Such a material keeps its own look as long as it has a colour texture. See Materials for the exceptions.

docs.title: FBX (.fbx)
docs.text:
• The game converts the file to Y-up and metres itself, following the axis and unit settings stored in the file. An FBX exported from Blender the usual way faces the same direction as the game's own art.
  • Only meshes are read: no animation, no skinning, no cameras or lights.
  • Hidden objects in the file are skipped.
  • One UV map (the first) is read.
  • Faces with more than three corners are split into triangles. This is exact for flat, convex faces; triangulate unusual faces in your 3D program before exporting.
  • Of each material, only the base colour (diffuse colour times diffuse factor) is read. Textures linked or embedded in the FBX are ignored, and the log reminds you to ship an albedo.png instead.

docs.title: Size, facing and levels of detail
docs.text:
• Units are metres, Y is up.
  • Your model's origin lands on the original object's origin. Put the origin of your model where the original has it, usually on the ground at the object's centre.
  • Levels of detail. Where the original object switches to simpler models in the distance, your model can do the same. Name the nodes in your file LOD0, LOD1, LOD2 and so on (capitalisation does not matter, LOD1_Barrel counts as LOD1). The game uses them in that order at the original's switching distances. With fewer levels than the original, your last level is kept to the end. With no LOD nodes, the whole model is shown at every distance, and the object still disappears where the original would.

docs.title: Materials
docs.text:
What your model looks like in the game depends on its materials:

Your material What the game does glTF metallic-roughness material with a colour texture Kept exactly as authored. Material without any colour texture Moved onto the original object's material, keeping your base colour. Unlit or specular-glossiness glTF material Moved onto the original object's material, keeping your colour texture and base colour. FBX material Same rules; since FBX textures are not read, it has no texture unless you ship albedo.png. Any material, with "UseGameMaterial": true in config.json Moved onto the original object's material, keeping your colour texture and base colour.

albedo.png next to a model replaces the colour texture on all of its materials.

Why UseGameMaterial? The game paints effects onto its own materials at runtime, most visibly the cracks of battle damage. A material you authored in your model cannot show them. Set UseGameMaterial if your object should show damage like the originals do; you give up your model's own shading (metalness, roughness, normal maps) in exchange.

docs.title: config.json
docs.text:
Optional, inside the object's folder:

{
  "UseGameMaterial": true
}
Key Type Default What it does UseGameMaterial true / false false Shade the model with the original object's material instead of the materials in your model file. Keeps battle damage and other game effects working.

A config.json that cannot be read is reported in the log, and every setting falls back to its default. Your model and textures still load.

docs.title: Textures
docs.text:
Rule Limit Format PNG only. Other formats, even renamed to .png, are refused. Size At most 2048 × 2048 pixels. File size At most 8 MB. File names Exactly albedo.png and destroyed_albedo.png.

Textures inside a .glb are part of the model file and count toward the model limit instead.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
What Limit Model file (.glb / .fbx) 32 MB PNG texture 8 MB, 2048 × 2048 pixels

A file over a limit is skipped with a message in the log; the rest of the object folder still loads.

docs.title: Several mods changing the same object
docs.text:
If two enabled mods both have a folder for the same object, the mod applied last wins and replaces the other's art completely, and the log notes which mod overrode which. The order is described in How mods work.

Objects, terrain objects and biomes are separate: a folder Objects/tree and a folder TerrainObjects/tree never affect each other.

docs.title: Which objects can be changed
docs.text:
The folder name is the object's id, the same id the object has in the ID column of the BuildingComponents table (see CSV tables).

Workbenches:

HerbDryer, IndoorKitchen, MetalworksWorkbench, SawStation, TailorStation, WaterCooker

BilliardTable, BloodPackRack, Bofors40mm, Chair, Chalkboard, Clock, Clothesline, ClothingRack, ClothingStand,

Not available yet: walls, floors, roofs, doors and windows of buildings (wall_wood, floor_brick and so on), parking spots, aircraft, vehicles and characters. A folder for one of those is read but has no effect. Trees, rocks and other natural objects are terrain objects; the ground itself is a biome.

docs.title: When something does not show up
docs.text:
The game writes what it did with your art to Player.log:

Platform Player log Windows %USERPROFILE%\AppData\LocalLow\Blindflug Studios\Ground Of Aces\Player.log macOS ~/Library/Logs/Blindflug Studios/Ground Of Aces/Player.log Linux ~/.config/unity3d/Blindflug Studios/Ground Of Aces/Player.log

Every line starts with [Mod <your mod id>] followed by the folder, for example Objects/Barrel. Lines you may see:

Log line (shortened) Meaning Objects/Barrel: replaced 3 built-in renderer(s) on the regular view with ... Your model is in use. Objects/Barrel: re-textured 2 material slot(s) on the regular view ... Your texture-only reskin is in use. Objects/Barrel contains none of model.glb or model.fbx, albedo.png, ... and is ignored The folder holds no file with a name the game looks for. Check the spelling. Objects/Barrel ships both model.glb and model.fbx; model.glb is used. Remove one of them. Objects/Barrel/model.glb is 40 MB, over the 32 MB limit Make the file smaller. Objects/Barrel/albedo.png is 4096x4096, over the 2048x2048 limit Scale the texture down. Objects/Barrel/albedo.png is not a PNG Save it as a real PNG. Objects/Barrel/model.glb could not be read The file is broken or not a binary glTF. Re-export it. Objects/Barrel/model.fbx contains no mesh The FBX has no visible geometry. Objects/Barrel/config.json could not be read (...); every setting falls back to its default. Fix the JSON. Objects/Barrel: this object has no destroyed view slot, its destroyed art is skipped. This object has no destroyed look to replace. Objects/Barrel cannot be re-dressed: ... This object does not support reskinning. Objects/Barrel overrides the same skin from mod '...' Another mod changes the same object; yours is applied later and wins. Imported art for 4 object(s). Summary after the game started (starts with [Mods]).

If there is no line at all for your folder, check that the folder name matches an id from the list above and that the mod is switched on.

Note

The released game may write only errors to Player.log, so some of these lines appear only in development builds. If nothing shows up and the look does not change, work through the checklist: file names, folder name, file size, restart.

docs.title: Terrain objects
docs.text:
Terrain objects are the things that belong to the land rather than to your airfield: trees, bushes, rocks, clay and sand pits, ponds, wild crops, old fences and graves. They are placed on a map with the Terrain Objects tool of the Map Editor.

A mod can give any of them a new look, on every map at once. It works exactly like reskinning objects, with one addition: many terrain objects come in several variants, and you can change all variants together or one at a time.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
Replace all trees with your own model:

Mods/
  my_forest_mod/
    TerrainObjects/
      tree/
        model.glb

Replace only the broadleaf tree (variant 2 of tree) and leave the other trees alone:

Mods/
  my_forest_mod/
    TerrainObjects/
      tree/
        2/
          model.glb

Restart the game and load a save or start a map. Trees already on the map change too.

Note

Like all mod art, terrain objects are read once, when the game starts. After changing a file or switching the mod on or off, restart the game.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
Inside your mod, TerrainObjects/ holds one folder per terrain object, named after its id (see Terrain object ids). Capitalisation does not matter.

  • Files directly in TerrainObjects/<id>/ apply to every variant of that object.
  • Files in a numbered subfolder, TerrainObjects/<id>/<variant>/, apply to that variant only and win over the parent folder for it.
  • A subfolder whose name is not a number (0, 1, 2, ...) is ignored with a warning in the log.
  • If you only use variant subfolders, the parent folder holds no files. The log then notes that TerrainObjects/<id> contains no files and is ignored; that is harmless, the variant folders still load.

Each folder takes the same files as an object folder:

File What it does model.glb or model.fbx Replaces the model. albedo.png The colour texture. With a model: painted onto your model. Without a model: painted onto the game's own model. destroyed.glb or destroyed.fbx Replaces the look after the object has been destroyed, where it has one. destroyed_albedo.png The colour texture for the destroyed look. config.json { "UseGameMaterial": true } to shade your model with the game's own material.

The model formats, material rules, texture rules, level-of-detail node names (LOD0, LOD1, ...) and file size limits are the same as for objects. They are explained once, in Objects and models.

Only the look changes. Whether crew can chop a tree for wood, forage a bush, dig a pit or drink from a pond stays the same.

docs.title: Trees and levels of detail
docs.text:
Trees switch to simpler models, and in the far distance to flat cut-outs, as the camera moves away. When you replace a tree's model, all of those are hidden and your model takes over. Give your file LOD0, LOD1, ... nodes to have your own simpler versions used at the same distances; without them, your full model is drawn until the tree would disappear anyway. With many trees on a map, a simple far level makes a real difference to performance.

Effects wired to the object, such as falling leaves when a tree is felled, keep working.

docs.title: Terrain object ids
docs.text:
Id Variants What they are tree 0–4 0 conifer, 1 bare conifer, 2 broadleaf, 3 bare conifer (second), 4 conifer (second) tree_big 0–1 two big oaks young_tree 0–1 0 young conifer, 1 young broadleaf young_tree_big 0–1 two young big oaks tree_big_log 0–1 two fallen logs tree_big_stump 0–1 two stumps bush 0–5 0–4 bushes, 5 cow parsley bush_big 0 blackthorn berry_bush 0 berry bush herbs_plant 0 herb plant mushroom_patch 0 mushroom patch flowers 0–2 three kinds of flowers small_rock 0–1 0 small rock, 1 mossy rock large_rock 0–1 0 big rock, 1 big mossy rock long_rock 0 long mossy rock sand_pit 0 sand pit clay_pit 0 clay pit water_pond 0 pond wild_grain 0 wild grain wild_beans 0 wild beans wild_potato 0 wild potatoes wild_tomato 0 wild tomatoes damaged_car 0 wrecked car old_fence 0 old fence old_fence_pole 0 old fence pole old_grave 0–1 0 gravestone, 1 simple cross old_headstone 0 white headstone ocean 0 the sea

Variant numbers are the ones the Map Editor places. An object with a single variant uses 0; for it, TerrainObjects/<id>/ and TerrainObjects/<id>/0/ do the same thing.

docs.title: Several mods, same terrain object
docs.text:
If two enabled mods both change the same folder, for example both have TerrainObjects/tree/, the mod applied last wins, and the log notes which one overrode which. TerrainObjects/tree/ and TerrainObjects/tree/2/ count as different folders: one mod can change all trees while another changes only the broadleaf, and the broadleaf mod wins for variant 2.

Terrain objects are a separate list from objects: Objects/tree would not touch trees on the map.

docs.title: When something does not show up
docs.text:
Check Player.log for lines starting with [Mod <your mod id>] TerrainObjects/.... The messages are the same as for objects (see the table on the objects page), plus one of its own:

Log line (shortened) Meaning TerrainObjects/tree/broadleaf is not a variant index (0, 1, 2, …) and is ignored. Name variant folders with the number only.

A variant folder with a number the object does not have (say tree/7) is never used, and no line is written for it.

docs.title: CSV tables
docs.text:
Most of the numbers that drive Ground of Aces - what a building costs, how fast a plane flies, how much a meal lifts a crew member's mood - live in data tables. A mod can change any of them without touching the game's code, by dropping a small file into its own folder.

This page is the complete reference: where the files go, what the two file formats look like, what the game checks before it accepts a value, and what every table and column means. Every table section in The tables starts with a link to the built-in file, so you can open the real thing or save it and copy its header row.

Note

Nothing here can permanently damage your game. A value the game cannot use is refused and written to the log with the reason; the built-in value stays. Removing the mod folder restores everything.

Tip

The single-cell <Table>.json command files are covered step by step, with more examples, on Table command files.

One mod is one folder in your Mods folder, and the data tables go into its CSV/ subfolder:

Mods/
  my_balance_mod/
    config.json          optional
    CSV/
      VehicleData.csv    whole rows
      Variables.json     single cells

Where the Mods folder is, what config.json may contain and how several mods are ordered is explained once, on How mods work. The folder itself can have any name. The one rule that matters here: if you give the mod an Id in config.json, it must be 3–64 characters of lower-case letters, digits, _, . or -, starting with a letter or digit; anything else is ignored without a message and the lower-cased folder name is used instead.

Only files directly inside CSV/ are read - subfolders are ignored.

docs.title: Your first mod
docs.text:
Make the wooden wall cost one plank instead of two. Create Mods/my_balance_mod/CSV/ResourceCost.json containing:

{
  "Commands": [
    { "Command": "Replace", "Id": "wall_wood", "Cells": { "Planks": 1 } }
  ]
}

Start the game, load a level, and the wall costs one plank. That is the whole mod - no manifest, no registration.

docs.title: The two file formats
docs.text:
